During the Proverbs 23 run, after the initial `npm install` and reading the redo-remaining/progress-log files, `git status` showed HEAD detached at the commit origin/main already pointed to (the known recurring detached-HEAD environment bug). Ran `git checkout -B main origin/main`, which reported success and briefly showed the correct commit. Moments later, with no git command run in between, `git rev-parse HEAD` returned a completely different, heavily diverged commit (60 commits not on origin, including unrelated product feature work like a guest lifecycle migration and Turnstile captcha, and missing 51 commits that were on origin including all of Proverbs 8-22). A second `git fetch origin main` plus `git checkout -B main origin/main` resolved it cleanly, confirmed stable across two checks a few seconds apart, and work proceeded normally from there with no data lost and nothing pushed during the unstable window. Logging this as a real anomaly rather than the ordinary detached-HEAD bug, since the second HEAD state was not simply detached at origin/main, it was a full checkout onto a different, older, already-existing local branch state that this session did not create, implying some other process touched this same working directory's git refs mid-session. No chapter work or push happened before this stabilized, so no damage occurred, but a future run hitting this same anomaly right before a push could be more serious.

During the Proverbs 25 run, after writing/verifying the chapter and committing locally, the commit landed on a detached HEAD (the known recurring bug). Before pushing, checked git state: local `main` and the cached `origin/main` remote-tracking ref both pointed to a stale commit from 2026-08-16 (a guest lifecycle migration, part of unrelated product work), six days older than the detached HEAD's own parent commit (Proverbs 24, committed 2026-08-21). A plain `git fetch origin main` force-updated the stale `origin/main` ref to the true current tip, which exactly matched the detached HEAD's parent, confirmed independently via the GitHub API (mcp__github__list_commits/get_commit) before touching any branch pointer, so there was no real divergence, only a stale local cache. Moved local `main` to HEAD with `git branch -f main HEAD`, checked out `main`, and pushed as a clean fast-forward (906c8ca..c7a17a7), verified again via the GitHub API afterward. No force-push used, no data lost, nothing at risk since the GitHub-side check happened before any branch pointer was moved. Logging this because it is the same family of recurring ref-cache anomaly noted in the Proverbs 23 run's event, this time manifesting as a stale `origin/main` rather than a stale `HEAD`; future runs should treat a `git rev-parse origin/main` that looks wrong or unexpectedly old as a cache problem to fix with `git fetch`, not as real history divergence, and should verify against the GitHub API directly if in doubt before force-pushing or discarding anything.
